title: Bata India Ltd - 500043 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Bata India posted a second straight quarter of 5%+ value growth in Q4 FY26; like-to-like PBT grew about 11% after excluding four non-cash items.
summary.overview: Management reported a second consecutive quarter of accelerating, volume-backed growth of 5%+ in value, with broad-based growth across channels and categories. Reported PBT fell about 94% due to exceptional items, mainly a plant closure (VRS) cost and a INR220 million FX impact on a licensing liability. Excluding four non-cash items, like-to-like PBT grew about 11% and cash flow from operations grew about 18%. Inventory fell 13% YoY and 28% over two years while availability rose about 1,000 bps, and ZBM stores were scaled to about 700 by May 2026.

segments.name: Retail (COCO/ZBM)
segments.commentary: Volume-led DOS growth; ZBM stores at about 550 last quarter with about 50-55% of COCO sales, rising to about 700 stores (about 70% of sales) by end-May 2026. Target of 800-850 stores by quarter end.

segments.name: Franchise (FOFO)
segments.commentary: Franchise stores crossed 700 with double-digit growth and higher overall profitability; franchise share is close to double digit of revenue. Management targets nearing 1,000 stores in the next 12 months.

segments.name: Multi-brand distribution (MBO)
segments.commentary: Expanded to about 1,670 towns; channel is showing early signs of growth after pressure in towns below 1,000. Distribution is about 10-12% of revenue.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Fastest-growing channel across B2B, B2C and dot-com; about 8-10% of revenue per CFO, about 12-13% per CEO. Over 700 stores fulfil online orders.

segments.name: Brands: Hush Puppies and Power/HP premium
segments.commentary: Hush Puppies is about 18-20% of turnover and the fastest-growing brand. Premium HP and Power portfolio is outpacing overall growth.

segments.name: Under INR1,000 MRP segment
segments.commentary: About 35-40% of revenue; declined for about 3 years but has stabilised and is now growing roughly in line with the overall ~5% top line.

guidance_outlook: Inventory is about 70-75% of the way through the reduction programme, with a target turn of about 3 versus about 2.7 currently, without compromising availability.
Full-price sales are growing about 2x overall growth; management is 'reasonably hopeful' of gross margin improvement going forward.
Raw material inflation is about 5-6% blended as of the last review; price increases of 5-6% are planned but not yet rolled out.
Franchise store count to approach 1,000 within about 12 months; ZBM stores to reach about 800-850 by the current quarter end.
Management declined to give forward-looking guidance on bata.com or overall D2C growth for FY27.
capex_capacity: One manufacturing facility closed in the quarter, with a related VRS exceptional cost; management is removing legacy factories and consolidating to a few large suppliers.
Store network is about 2,000 EBOs (COCO plus franchise), with about 1,150 COCO stores.
Marketing spend is about 1.5x prior levels, with digital about 80-85% of the spend.
Sneakers proposition under development to target younger consumers; details to be shared later.
demand_pricing: March was better than January, and management sees no tangible change in consumer sentiment as of now, but will not give forward-looking statements.
Brand consideration rose to 66, its highest level; Ballerina campaign drew a strong response.
Full-price sales are growing faster, with markdowns lower; gross margin optics are diluted by franchise mix and a one-off INR60 million provision reversal in the base quarter.
Trade receivables rose about 65% YoY, attributed to channel mix (wholesale, franchise, B2B e-commerce) and base effect; management says provisions for doubtful debts show no deterioration.
Minimum wage hikes in Haryana, UP and Karnataka are seen as structural; the company is spread across 30 states and only 3-4 are affected so far.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory at a desirable level, and why is lower discounting not showing in gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Turns are about 2.7 against a target of about 3. Gross margin optics are diluted by the shift to franchise (lower GM%, accretive to EBIT) and a INR60 million provision reversal in base Q4 FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What raw material and minimum wage impact is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended raw material inflation is about 5-6% and is being covered by inventory, hedges and price elasticity-led pricing. Management sees no direct impact yet, and wage hikes are structural but partly offset because many stores already pay above minimum wage.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the Bata brand's revenue growth been stagnant, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to inventory simplification, which had deteriorated and is now recovering, along with franchise expansion, SIS, digital, and product and marketing levers.

qa_highlights.question: How long will vendor and store revamps take to reach the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees underlying operating leverage coming through from store revamp, inventory decluttering and supplier consolidation, with benefits in coming periods.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise about 65% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Due to channel mix, with more credit in wholesale, franchise and B2B e-commerce, plus a base effect. Management says the quality is fine and doubtful-debt provisions are steady.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue split between below and above INR1,000 products, and what is Hush Puppies' contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Below INR1,000 is about 35-40% of revenue and has stabilised. Hush Puppies is about 18-20% of turnover. Management will provide the exact split offline, and it could not give FY25/FY26 volume growth on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the channel mix?
qa_highlights.answer: COCO is about 65% and non-COCO about 35%. Within non-COCO, franchise is close to double digit, e-commerce about 8-10% and distribution about 10-12%.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation of 5-6% with price hikes not yet rolled out; crude oil and war-related disruption could change this.
Gross margin recovery is not yet visible because of franchise mix and one-off base effects.
Trade receivables up about 65% YoY, linked to fast-growing wholesale, franchise and B2B e-commerce credit.
Recurring non-cash items and exceptional charges (plant closure, FX on licence liability, lease gains falling) affect reported PBT.
Execution risk on ZBM rollout to 800-850 stores, franchise to about 1,000, and launch of the sneakers proposition.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum, ZBM and franchise expansion, and inventory discipline, but cautious and non-committal on forward numbers (no FY27 guidance, no bata.com or price-hike quantum). Management was less precise on several detailed data points, deferring some to offline follow-up.
